hook_1.message: Take a look at these two bars. Something is similar and something is different.

hook_confirm.message: Exactly! Different number of pieces, but the colored part is the same size. That's today's big idea.

hook_more_pieces.message: Right — the bottom bar has more pieces. But look at the colored parts. They end at the same spot!

hook_look_different.message: They do look different! But look at just the colored parts. They take up the same amount of space.

define_1.message: When two fractions look different but mean the same amount, they're called equivalent fractions.

define_2.message: 1/2 and 2/4 are equivalent. Different numbers, same amount colored.

why_1.message: Why does this matter? Imagine you're baking and need 1/2 a cup of sugar — but you only have a 1/4 cup.

why_2.message: How many 1/4 cups would you need to make 1/2?

why_confirm.message: Two 1/4 cups equals 1/2 cup. You just used equivalent fractions! Now let's learn how to find them.

why_hint.message: Look at the bars — 2 out of 4 pieces equals 1 out of 2. So two 1/4 cups makes 1/2 cup!

shade_teach.message: Let's start fresh. Here's one whole bar. Tap it to color it in!

shade_wait.message: Tap the bar to color it.
shade_wait.hint: Just tap once on the bar!

shade_confirm.message: Nice! That's one whole — 1 out of 1 piece colored.

cut_intro.message: Now watch what happens when I cut it into 2 equal pieces.

cut_reveal.message: I cut it but didn't change how much is colored. 1 out of 2 pieces — that's 1/2. Make sense?

cut_explain.message: The bar has 2 pieces now. 1 is colored. That's 1 out of 2 — we write it as 1/2!

cut_confirm.message: Here's the secret: when you cut a bar into more pieces, you can find a new fraction that means the same thing.

split_teach.message: Your turn! Here's a second bar below. Tap a piece twice quickly to cut it in half.

split_wait.message: Double-tap a piece in the blue bar to cut it!
split_wait.hint: Tap the same piece two times quickly.

split_confirm.message: You cut it! See how one piece became two? Now keep cutting until you have 4 pieces, then color 2 of them.

equiv_wait_1.message: Make the blue bar show 2/4 — four pieces, two colored.
equiv_wait_1.hint: Cut pieces until you have 4, then tap 2 of them to color.

equiv_reveal_1.message: Look at that — the colored parts on both bars end at the same spot!

equiv_confirm_1.message: Yes! You just found an equivalent fraction by cutting into more pieces. The colored amount stayed the same.

equiv_misconception_1.message: The numbers are bigger, but look at the bars. The colored parts are the same size. More pieces just means smaller pieces!

equiv_hint_1.message: Look at where the color stops on each bar. They line up — same space, same amount!

challenge_2_setup.message: Let's try a harder one. The top bar shows 2/3. Can you make the bottom bar equivalent?

challenge_2_wait.message: Cut and color the purple bar until it matches 2/3.
challenge_2_wait.hint: Try making 6 pieces and coloring 4. See if it lines up!

challenge_2_reveal.message: The colored parts line up again — you found another equivalent fraction!

pattern_question.message: We keep cutting into more pieces but the colored amount stays the same. Why does that work?

pattern_confirm.message: That's the secret! When you cut into more pieces, each piece gets smaller — but you color more of them. It balances out.

pattern_redirect.message: The numbers do change. But the colored part doesn't! More pieces, smaller pieces, more of them colored — it evens out.

pattern_explain.message: Think of cutting a pizza slice in half. You have more pieces, but the same amount of pizza! That's what happens here.

non_example_setup.message: But not all fractions are equivalent. Let's check — is 1/2 the same as 1/3?

non_example_question.message: Look at where the color ends on each bar. Same spot or different?

non_example_correct.message: Right! The colors don't line up, so they're not equivalent. The bars always tell the truth.

non_example_wrong.message: Look closely — the teal color goes further than the coral. 1/2 is more than 1/3!

non_example_misconception.message: 3 is a bigger number, but more pieces means each piece is smaller. 1 out of 3 is less than 1 out of 2!

non_example_why.message: We didn't just cut into more pieces here — we also changed how many are colored. That's why they're not equivalent.

assessment_intro.message: Time to test your skills! Three quick questions.

quiz_1_right.message: 3 out of 6 — the colored parts line up with 1 out of 2!

quiz_1_wrong.message: Look — 1/2 and 3/6 line up perfectly. Same amount, different pieces!

quiz_2_right.message: 4 out of 6 matches 2 out of 3 — each top piece equals two bottom pieces!

quiz_2_wrong.message: See — 4/6 lines up with 2/3. Cut each piece in half and you get the same amount colored!

quiz_3_right.message: 2 colored vs 3 colored — the bars don't line up, so they're not equivalent!

quiz_3_wrong.message: 2 pieces colored vs 3 — that's a different amount! The bars don't line up.

complete.message: You did it! Remember — if the colored parts line up, the fractions are equivalent. You're a fraction explorer now!
